questions.q: What does IIF(ListPrice > 1000, 'Premium', 'Standard') return when ListPrice is 1500?
options: 'Premium'
'Standard'
NULL
An error, because IIF needs a third branch
questions.explain: The condition ListPrice > 1000 is TRUE, so IIF returns the true_value, 'Premium'.

questions.q: Which CASE expression is IIF(condition, a, b) exactly equivalent to?
options: CASE WHEN condition THEN a ELSE b END
CASE WHEN condition THEN b ELSE a END
CASE WHEN a THEN condition ELSE b END
There is no equivalent CASE expression
questions.explain: IIF is direct shorthand for a two-branch CASE: the true_value maps to THEN, the false_value maps to ELSE.

questions.q: What does IIF return when its condition evaluates to NULL or UNKNOWN?
options: The false_value, just like a CASE expression's WHEN treats a non-TRUE condition
The true_value
NULL, regardless of either branch
A runtime error
questions.explain: IIF mirrors CASE's WHEN logic exactly — only a TRUE condition takes the true_value branch.

questions.q: Why is nesting IIF for three or more branches usually a sign to switch to CASE?
options: Nested IIF calls get hard to read fast, while CASE stays readable with multiple WHEN clauses
Nested IIF is not valid T-SQL syntax
IIF can only be nested up to two levels before SQL Server rejects it
CASE runs faster than nested IIF at execution time
questions.explain: Both compile to the same thing internally, so it's purely a readability tradeoff — CASE scales to multiple branches more clearly.

questions.q: What SQL Server version introduced IIF, and why was it added?
options: SQL Server 2012, as shorthand for a familiar two-branch conditional pattern from tools like Excel and Access
SQL Server 2000, as the original form of CASE
SQL Server 2022, to support JSON functions
IIF has always existed since SQL Server's first release
questions.explain: IIF arrived in SQL Server 2012 as convenience syntax sugar that compiles down to an equivalent CASE expression.
